operational_definition: Structural information asymmetry is the extent to which the event-generation process creates materially unequal information sets before public/common revelation. IAS measures that structure; feasibility is evaluated separately.

PAC.name: Privileged Access Concentration

anchors.0: No process-based earlier access to decisive state; decisive information is public.
anchors.1: Only public latency/technology advantage; no restricted material state.
anchors.2: Earlier access is diffuse across many actors or concerns partial non-decisive state.
anchors.3: A bounded multi-party set has documented earlier access to material partial state.
anchors.4: A small bounded set has earlier access to material or near-decisive state.
anchors.5: A highly concentrated decision/control set knows or determines decisive state well before public revelation.

PAC.safety: PAC is a structural process score and never implies illegal conduct by a named person.

anchors.0: Outcome is mechanical from continuously public observables.
anchors.1: Mostly public state with only a minor/short latent component.
anchors.2: Material latent state exists but frequent public updates strongly constrain it.
anchors.3: Decisive state is materially latent between intermittent public updates.
anchors.4: Most decisive state develops inside a private, internal, negotiation, or regulatory process.
anchors.5: Decisive state is fundamentally opaque until a discrete reveal.

anchors.1: Basic domain knowledge or simple threshold interpretation.
anchors.2: Professional finance/statistics knowledge using standard tools.
anchors.3: Substantial domain expertise and multi-source synthesis required.
anchors.4: Narrow scientific, legal, technical, or regulatory specialist expertise required.
anchors.5: Highly specialized case-specific interpretation remains difficult even for outside professionals.

TAW.name: Temporal Asymmetry Window
TAW.definition: Duration for which a meaningful unequal-information state can plausibly exist; never prediction-market contract lead time.

PSI.name: Public Saturation Inverse

anchors.0: Near-continuous dense monitoring and standardized forecasts across multiple independent public channels.
anchors.1: Dense consensus, multiple public signals, and broad coverage.
anchors.2: Broad coverage and standardized forecasts, but meaningful idiosyncratic uncertainty remains.
anchors.4: Sparse specialist coverage and limited standardized forecasts.
anchors.5: Little or no standardized pre-event forecasting apparatus.

PSI.low_anchor_evidence_rule: Scores 0 or 1 require at least two distinct public information/forecast channels.

construct_boundary.reason: These determine testability, execution, or evidence confidence rather than structural asymmetry itself.

A.meaning: Direct same-family high-quality evidence plus strong institutional/process support or independent corroboration.
A.sampling: triangular clipped to [0,5] around anchor with half-width 0.5

B.meaning: Strong same-family mechanism/evidence with a material directness or coverage limitation.
B.sampling: triangular clipped to [0,5] around anchor with half-width 1.0

C.sampling: triangular clipped to [0,5] around anchor with half-width 2.0

D.sampling: anchor must be null; Uniform(0,5); family/dimension remains unresolved rather than scored low.

evidence_gate.effect: Families failing this gate cannot support a comparative highest-asymmetry claim or W3 protocol eligibility.

central_aggregation.rule: IAS_central=(PAC+LSO+SIB+TAW+PSI)/5 only when no ECG-D is present.
central_aggregation.scale_assumption: Operational 0-5 levels are treated as approximately equally spaced for the central index; sensitivity analysis is mandatory.

smaa.weight_distribution: Dirichlet(1,1,1,1,1), uniform over the full five-dimensional simplex
smaa.robust_high_requirement: IAS_central>=3 and P(IAS>=3)>=0.75 and evidence gate passes.

taxonomy_rule: Do not merge/split a family after real scoring to improve rank or feasibility. Any post-freeze taxonomy change becomes exploratory/new-version work.

F3_sampleability_floor.semantics: Floor authorizes W3 protocol drafting only; it is not a claim of statistical power.

multi_candidate_selection.practical_IAS_tie: All eligible families within strictly less than 0.05 rank-1 acceptability of the top eligible family.
multi_candidate_selection.claim_rule: Feasibility tie-breaking selects a future experiment only; it does not create a highest-asymmetry claim when comparative-claim gate fails.

forbidden_inputs: linked-asset realized returns used to choose families
discovery_firewall.missing_discovery_semantics: Missing or low discovery is FEASIBILITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED, never IAS=0.

references.source: OECD/JRC Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators

freeze_rule: Freeze only after byte-level review of this draft plus synthetic validator. Any substantive change requires a new version and complete synthetic revalidation before real-family scoring.
